object_description: dominant three-story volume with attached pent roofs
design_condition: The main volume follows the existing school complex and encloses a courtyard with a low connecting building, but its proximity and scale beside the church and village square make the urban setting difficult to imagine.

positive.statement: The break area is clearly defined, with a paved circulation zone, gravel area, trees, and a covered bicycle shelter.

position.rationale: The break area is approximated in the open zone between the main masses.

positive.statement: The main entrances are easy to find and grouped under the large canopy.

position.rationale: Entrances are placed along the lower edge of the dominant volume beneath its projected canopy.

positive.statement: The community hall foyer is spacious, well lit on both sides, and directly connected to the inner courtyard.

position.target: community hall foyer and inner courtyard
position.rationale: The foyer is approximated at the central connection between hall volume and courtyard.

positive.statement: All rooms in the halls are correctly placed and well developed.

position.rationale: Hall rooms are distributed within the eastern sampled volume, though interiors are not separable.

positive.statement: The slightly sloping roofs adopt familiar elements from the neighborhood and integrate well with them.

position.rationale: Roof profiles and their stepped massing are visible across the elevations.

positive.statement: The materialization with color-treated wooden parts is appropriate for the location and easy to imagine.

position.rationale: Material treatment is anchored to the exposed facade of the dominant volume.

negative.statement: The three-story house appears as a strongly dominating volume despite being set back from the cemetery and church.

position.rationale: The tall left-hand volume dominates the elevations and plan.

negative.statement: The proximity of the four-story main building to the church and village square is problematic and represents a missed opportunity.

position.target: main building beside church and village square
position.rationale: The dominant volume is placed toward the village-square-facing southern side.

negative.statement: The height of the village square and the entrance to the parish hall is questioned.

position.target: village square and parish hall entrance height
position.rationale: The entrance-height concern is anchored to the lower open edge near the square.

negative.statement: The possible internal connection between the halls would also be questionable.

position.rationale: The central link between the two visible masses is the plausible connection location.

negative.statement: The project remains too closely linked to the existing building.

position.rationale: The connector zone is used as the approximate interface with the existing building.
